title: Is High Calcium a Sign of Cancer? What a High Result Usually Means
summary: Is high calcium a sign of cancer? Why an overactive parathyroid is the usual cause, which cancers raise calcium, what level is urgent, and how PTH tells them apart.
body_markdown:
Table of contents


High calcium on a routine blood test is usually not a sign of cancer. The most common cause of high blood calcium is primary hyperparathyroidism, in which one or more of the four small parathyroid glands in the neck makes too much parathyroid hormone (PTH) ([Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/hypercalcemia-of-malignancy) ). Cancer can raise calcium, but this usually happens late in the course of a cancer that is already causing other symptoms. The test that separates the two is PTH measured alongside calcium.


For the full list of causes and symptoms of a high result, see[high calcium symptoms and causes](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-high-calcium) . For what the numbers mean, see the[calcium](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/calcium) ,[corrected calcium](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/corrected-calcium) and[parathyroid hormone](https://mitohealth.com/biomarkers/parathyroid-hormone-pth) overviews. This page answers one question: could a high calcium mean cancer, and how do you find out?


## The short answer


- **Parathyroid disease is the usual cause.** Primary hyperparathyroidism and cancer together account for more than 90% of high calcium, and cancer is the most common cause in people who are in hospital ([StatPearls](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29494030/) ). A review in American Family Physician calls primary hyperparathyroidism the most common cause of high calcium, and says it is most often found by chance in people without symptoms ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ).
- **Cancer that raises calcium is rarely hidden.** In people whose cancer has raised their calcium, symptoms of the cancer are usually already present when the high calcium is found. Occasionally, a high calcium found by chance is the first sign ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ).
- **PTH tells them apart.** With a parathyroid cause, PTH is high or stays in the normal range when it should have fallen. With cancer, PTH is low or suppressed ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ;[Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ).
- **Some highs are not real, or have a simple explanation.** Dehydration, and medicines or supplements such as thiazide water pills, lithium, vitamin D and calcium, can all play a part.


## How cancer raises calcium


Cancer raises blood calcium in a few distinct ways. Each points to a different group of cancers, and each leaves a different pattern on blood tests.


- **A hormone made by the tumor (PTHrP).** Some tumors release parathyroid hormone-related peptide (PTHrP), which acts like PTH and pulls calcium out of bone. Sources estimate this causes about 80% of high calcium in cancer. It is most linked with squamous cell cancers, such as those of the lung, head and neck, and esophagus, and with breast and kidney cancers ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ;[Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ).
- **Cancer in the bone.** Tumor cells that spread to bone, or grow in the bone marrow, break bone down and release calcium. This route accounts for about 20% of cases and occurs mainly with multiple myeloma and breast cancer ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ).
- **Extra active vitamin D.** Some lymphomas turn vitamin D into its active form, calcitriol, which increases calcium absorption from food. It is the main cause of high calcium in Hodgkin lymphoma ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ). Sarcoidosis and some infections, which are not cancers, do the same thing.
- **A tumor that makes PTH itself.** This is the rarest route, at under 1% of cancer-related cases.


The cancers most often behind high calcium are multiple myeloma, then breast cancer, kidney cancer and squamous cell cancers ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ). Multiple myeloma deserves a note because it can be found through blood tests: the National Cancer Institute lists bone pain, especially in the back or ribs, bones that break easily, frequent infections, and tiredness among its signs, and explains that myeloma can damage bone and raise calcium ([NCI](https://www.cancer.gov/types/myeloma/patient/myeloma-treatment-pdq) ).


These proportions come from reviews of people already known to have cancer, and they vary between studies. A 2021 cohort cited in the same review found bone involvement and active vitamin D more often than the classic figures suggest ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ). They describe how cancer raises calcium. They do not tell you how likely cancer is when your own calcium is high.


## What calcium level is concerning, and when it is urgent


No calcium level on its own diagnoses cancer. What the level does tell you is how quickly you need care. StatPearls groups high calcium into three bands ([StatPearls](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29494030/) ):


Band Total calcium


Mild Above normal, below 12 mg/dL


Moderate 12 to 14 mg/dL


Severe Above 14 mg/dL


Primary hyperparathyroidism usually causes mild, stable high calcium, and it is often found in people with no symptoms ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ). People whose high calcium comes from cancer usually have higher levels and more severe symptoms ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ). The American Family Physician review names low PTH, symptoms that come on quickly, and signs such as weight loss without trying, loss of appetite, tiredness and night sweats as the pattern that should raise the question ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ).


Get medical care promptly, the same day, if a high calcium comes with confusion, marked weakness, vomiting, heavy thirst, or reduced urine. These are among the symptoms of high calcium from cancer ([Higdon et al., 2018](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30215936/) ), and very high calcium can cause kidney failure, abnormal heart rhythm, confusion and coma ([Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/hypercalcemia-of-malignancy) ). A result in the moderate or severe band also needs prompt medical evaluation rather than a wait for more tests. The[high calcium page](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-high-calcium) covers the other symptoms.


## Can you have high calcium without cancer?


Yes, and most people with a high calcium on a routine test do. MedlinePlus names excess PTH from the parathyroid glands as the most common cause, usually from a growth that is benign ([MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000365.htm) ). In about 8 out of 10 people with primary hyperparathyroidism, the cause is a single benign tumor called an adenoma ([NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/primary-hyperparathyroidism) ). It is one of the most common hormone disorders, most often affects people between 50 and 60, and is 3 to 4 times more common in women than men.


Primary hyperparathyroidism still matters. Over time it can thin bones and cause kidney stones ([Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/hypercalcemia-of-malignancy) ), and it is often treated with surgery ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ). But it is a different conversation from a cancer workup.


One more benign cause is worth knowing about. Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia is a rare inherited condition that causes lifelong high calcium with normal or slightly high PTH and low calcium in the urine. It generally needs no treatment, including surgery ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ).


## False highs and medicines


Before looking for a disease, check whether the result reflects how calcium is carried in the blood, your fluid status, or something you take.


- **Albumin affects how total calcium reads.** About 40% to 45% of blood calcium is bound to albumin, so total calcium rises and falls with albumin. Low albumin lowers measured total calcium, which can hide a true high rather than create one. That is why total calcium is often corrected for albumin, and an ionized (free) calcium test measures the active form directly ([StatPearls](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29494030/) ). MedlinePlus notes that ionized calcium is usually ordered when total calcium is abnormal ([MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/calcium-blood-test/) ). In myeloma, abnormal proteins can also bind calcium, which is one more reason ionized calcium is preferred there ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ).
- **Dehydration.** Calcium can read high when the body is low on fluids ([MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000365.htm) ).
- **Thiazide water pills.** The FDA label for hydrochlorothiazide says thiazides may cause slight, intermittent rises in calcium, that marked high calcium may point to hidden hyperparathyroidism, and that thiazides should be stopped before parathyroid function tests ([FDA label via DailyMed](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=01ad3531-5ed9-434c-b7d5-02d72aa82e46) ). That stop is a decision for the prescriber.
- **Lithium.** The FDA label for lithium links long-term use with persistent hyperparathyroidism and high calcium that may not resolve after lithium is stopped. It also notes that dehydration from lithium’s effect on the kidneys can cause a false mild high ([FDA label via DailyMed](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=01c4facd-ed79-4078-ba33-2044de372d0f) ).
- **Vitamin D and calcium supplements.** Too much vitamin D over a long time raises calcium ([MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/calcium-blood-test/) ). Very large amounts of calcium supplements together with high doses of vitamin D cause milk-alkali syndrome ([MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/000365.htm) ). Vitamin A and teriparatide or abaloparatide, used for osteoporosis, are also on the list ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ).


Bring a full list of medicines and supplements to whoever reviews your result. Many of these explanations are found that way.


## Which tests come next


Each test answers a different question, and the order matters.


Test Question it answers What the result suggests


[Calcium with PTH](https://mitohealth.com/products/ca-pth-intact) Is the high calcium coming from the parathyroid glands? High or normal PTH with high calcium points to primary hyperparathyroidism. Low PTH points away from the parathyroid glands ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) ;[MedlinePlus](https://medlineplus.gov/lab-tests/parathyroid-hormone-pth-test/) ;[Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) )


[Ionized calcium](https://mitohealth.com/products/calcium-ionized) Is the high real, independent of albumin? Measures the active, unbound calcium ([StatPearls](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29494030/) )


[Vitamin D, 25-hydroxy](https://mitohealth.com/products/vitamin-d-25-hydroxy-calcidiol) Is vitamin D intake involved? Part of the standard first workup of high calcium, alongside albumin, creatinine and urine calcium ([Sell et al., 2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35289573/) )


PTHrP, protein electrophoresis, active vitamin D (through a clinician) Is a cancer-related process involved? Ordered when PTH is low. High PTHrP supports a tumor hormone cause, and blood protein studies look for myeloma ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ;[NCI](https://www.cancer.gov/types/myeloma/patient/myeloma-treatment-pdq) )


A few points explain the order:


- **Start with calcium and PTH together.** Because primary hyperparathyroidism is the most common cause, the first diagnostic step is to measure PTH ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ). A high calcium should switch PTH off, so a PTH that is high or still normal is the signature of the parathyroid glands ([Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/hypercalcemia-of-malignancy) ). The[PTH test on its own](https://mitohealth.com/products/parathyroid-hormone-pth-intact) works if you already have a same-day calcium, but PTH has to be read against calcium from the same draw.
- **Check vitamin D and ionized calcium next.** Vitamin D shows whether supplements are a factor, and low vitamin D is common in primary hyperparathyroidism ([NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/primary-hyperparathyroidism) ). Ionized calcium shows the true level when albumin is abnormal and the total is hard to read.
- **Leave PTHrP and protein studies to a clinician.** When PTH is low, the next tests depend on symptoms, examination and history, and may include imaging ([Endocrine Society](https://www.endocrine.org/patient-engagement/endocrine-library/hypercalcemia-of-malignancy) ). In someone without a known cancer, a low PTH with high calcium is the pattern that leads to a search for one ([Bartkiewicz et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11202131/) ), so a clinician should direct this step rather than a test-by-test search.


## What to ask a clinician


- Is my calcium still high on a repeat test, and was it corrected for albumin or measured as ionized calcium?
- What was my PTH from the same blood draw, and does it fit primary hyperparathyroidism?
- Could any of my medicines or supplements, such as a thiazide, lithium, vitamin D or calcium, be contributing, and should anything change before retesting?
- If PTH is low, which tests come next, and how soon?
- If this is primary hyperparathyroidism, do I meet the criteria for surgery, or should we monitor bones and kidneys?


## Next step


If your calcium is 12 mg/dL or higher, or a high result comes with confusion, vomiting, marked weakness or very little urine, get medical care promptly rather than ordering more tests. If you have a mildly high result from routine blood work, start with the[Calcium and PTH test](https://mitohealth.com/products/ca-pth-intact) . It measures total calcium and intact PTH from the same draw, which is the pairing that tells a parathyroid cause from the others. Add[ionized calcium](https://mitohealth.com/products/calcium-ionized) or[vitamin D](https://mitohealth.com/products/vitamin-d-25-hydroxy-calcidiol) when the first result points there. Mito orders the tests and a clinician reviews your results.


If your calcium came back low rather than high, see[low calcium symptoms and causes](https://mitohealth.com/symptom-levels/symptoms-of-low-calcium) .


## Frequently asked questions


### Can you have high calcium and not have cancer?


Yes, and that is the usual situation. Primary hyperparathyroidism, most often from a benign growth on one parathyroid gland, is the most common cause of high blood calcium. Thiazide water pills, lithium, too much vitamin D or calcium from supplements, and dehydration can also raise it.


### What level of calcium in the blood indicates cancer?


No calcium level diagnoses cancer. Calcium from cancer tends to be higher and rise faster than calcium from a parathyroid problem, but the cause is found with other tests, starting with parathyroid hormone (PTH). A high calcium with a low PTH points away from the parathyroid glands and needs a prompt workup.


### How long can a person live with high calcium levels?


It depends on the cause. MedlinePlus says the outlook is good for mild hyperparathyroidism and other treatable causes. When cancer causes high calcium, the cancer is usually advanced, so the outlook reflects the cancer more than the calcium, and the Endocrine Society notes that newer cancer treatments have markedly lowered the death rate linked with it.


### How do you bring calcium levels down?


Treatment depends on the cause, so finding the cause comes first. A parathyroid adenoma is usually removed surgically, a medicine or supplement may be adjusted by the prescriber, and very high calcium is treated in hospital with fluids through a vein and medicines that slow bone breakdown. Do not stop a prescribed medicine on your own because of a calcium result.
